question.text: What is the LOWEST risk level shown on the Risk-o-meter?

explanation.text: The Logic: On the SEBI Risk-o-meter, the lowest band is labelled "Low" — the scale runs Low → Low to Moderate → Moderate → Moderately High → High → Very High. The regulator deliberately avoids "Very Low" or "Zero Risk" because all mutual-fund schemes carry at least some market or credit risk; the bottom band acknowledges minimal but non-zero risk. The Trap: "Very Low" and "Minimal" are not labels used on the Risk-o-meter. "Zero Risk" is misleading because no mutual-fund scheme can be guaranteed risk-free; capital-protected and other very-low-risk schemes still sit in the "Low" band. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B (MFF) workbook supports the disclosure purpose of the Risk-o-meter but the pages checked do not explicitly name "Low" as the lowest level or list the six categories. The labelling above reflects general SEBI/industry usage of the current Risk-o-meter scale.
